message.content:
**Paris Trip Planner – A 7‑Day Adventure**

> *Assumptions:*  
> • You’re traveling from North America/Europe (no special visas).  
> • Budget range: **$1 200–2 500 USD** total (excluding flights).  
> • Ideal season: late March–early June or September–October (mild weather & fewer crowds).

---

### Day 0 – Arrival & Settling In  

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| Morning | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle / Orly → take RER B or airport shuttle into city center. Check into your hotel/apartment. |
| Afternoon | Light stroll along the Seine; grab croissants & coffee at **Café des Deux Moulins** (Montmartre). |
| Evening | Dinner near your lodging—try a classic French bistro such as **Le Petit Cler** (Latin Quarter) or **L’Avant Comptoir** (Marais). |

*Tip*: Get a **Navigo Week Pass** (€22.80) for unlimited metro/bus rides during your stay.

---

## Day 1 – Classic Icons

| Time | Attraction | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| 9:00 AM | Eiffel Tower | Book tickets online ahead of time (skip‑the‑line). Take photos from Trocadéro Gardens too. |
| 11:30 AM | Champ‑de‑Mars walk → Musée d’Orsay | Pre‑book museum entry (~€14). Enjoy Impressionist masterpieces. |
| 2:00 PM | Lunch at **Les Ombres** (terrace overlooking Notre‑Dame). |
| 3:45 PM | Notre‑Dame Cathedral & Île Saint-Louis | Explore the island’s cafés and bookshop “Shakespeare & Company.” |
| 6:00 PM | River cruise (Bateaux Parisiens) | Sunset views of illuminated landmarks. |
| 8:30 PM | Dinner in Latin Quarter – try **La Coupole** or **Chez L'Ami Jean**. |

---

## Day 2 – Art & Culture

| Time | Attraction | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| 10:00 AM | Louvre Museum | Reserve timed ticket (~€15). Focus on highlights: Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Winged Victory. |
| 1:00 PM | Picnic lunch in Jardin des Tuileries (grab baguette, cheese, wine). |
| 2:30 PM | Palais Royal & gardens | Browse chic boutiques around Rue Cambon. |
| 4:00 PM | Le Marais district | Visit Picasso Museum or Carnavalet Museum. |
| 6:30 PM | Walk across Pont Alexandre III back toward Hôtel de Ville. |
| 8:00 PM | Dinner at **Septime** (Michelin‑starred, reservation required). |

---

## Day 3 – Montmartre & Hidden Gems

| Time | Attraction | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| 9:30 AM | Sacré-Cœur Basilica | Climb up for panoramic view of Paris. |
| 11:00 AM | Place du Tertre artists' square | Watch painters sketch; buy souvenirs. |
| 12:30 PM | Lunch at **Le Consulat** (historic café). |
| 2:00 PM | Moulin Rouge area | Optional cabaret show booking ~€120 incl dinner. |
| 4:30 PM | Explore Canal Saint-Martin | Trendy shops, street art, relaxed vibe. |
| 7:00 PM | Dinner at **Frenchie To Go** (casual yet upscale). |

---

## Day 4 – Day Trip Options

Choose one based on interest:

| Option | Highlights | Approx Cost |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| **Versailles Palace** | Hall of Mirrors, Gardens, Grand Trianon | €20 train + €18 entrance |
| **Giverny (Monet's Garden)** | Water lily pond, house | €25 roundtrip bus + free garden |
| **Champagne Region (Reims/Tremblay)** | Champagne houses tour | €70–100 including tastings |

Return to Paris in evening; light supper nearby.

---

## Day 5 – Modern & Shopping

| Time | Attraction | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| 10:00 AM | Centre Pompidou | Contemporary art; rooftop terrace offers great skyline shots. |
| 12:30 PM | Lunch at **Pink Flamingo** (inside Pompidou). |
| 2:00 PM | Galeries Lafayette & Printemps | Window shop luxury brands; climb to roof terrace for sunset. |
| 4:30 PM | Stroll through Opéra Garnier courtyard | Free guided tours available. |
| 7:00 PM | Dinner at **Restaurant Guy Savoy** (optional splurge). |

---

## Day 6 – Relaxation & Nightlife

| Time | Plan |
|------|------|
| 9:00 AM | Brunch at **Holybelly** (Brooklyn‑style brunch spot). |
| 11:30 AM | Spa treatment at **Spa Nuxe** (budget-friendly). |
| 2:00 PM | Leisure walk in Luxembourg Gardens; perhaps rent a rowboat on the Medlar Pond. |
| 5:30 PM | Early dinner at **Le Cinq Codet** (modern French cuisine). |
| 7:30 PM | Attend a jazz club (**New Morning**, **Jazz Club Etoile**) or catch a performance at Théâtre Mogador. |
| 10:30 PM | Late-night dessert at **Berthillon Ice Cream** on Ile Saint-Louis. |

---

## Day 7 – Departure Prep

| Time | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| 9:00 AM | Pack last-minute items; double-check passport & boarding passes. |
| 11:00 AM | Quick souvenir shopping at **Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen** (flea market). |
| 1:00 PM | Farewell lunch at **Crêperie Josselin** (côte‑d’azur style crêpes). |
| 3:00 PM | Head to airport via RER B or taxi; leave ample buffer for security lines. |

---

### Packing Checklist

| Category | Essentials |
|-----------|------------|
| Clothing | Comfortable walking shoes, layers (spring/fall), scarf, hat, umbrella. |
| Tech | Phone charger, power adapter (Type E/F), portable battery pack. |
| Documents | Passport, flight tickets, insurance card, emergency contacts. |
| Misc | Reusable water bottle, small backpack, notebook, phrasebook (“Bonjour”, “Merci”). |

---

### Money Matters

| Item | Typical Price Range |
|------|---------------------|
| Hotel (mid‑range) | $150–250/night |
| Meals (average) | Breakfast ~$10, Lunch ~$15, Dinner ~$35 |
| Attractions | Most museums €13–€16; skip‑the‑line tickets extra €5–€10 |
| Transport | Navigo week pass €22.80; single metro ride €1.90 |
| Souvenirs | Miniature Eiffel Tower €10–€20; perfume €50+ |

Total estimate for 7 nights ≈ **$1 800–$2 300** excluding airfare.

---

### Safety Tips

1. **Pickpocket vigilance:** Keep wallets in front pockets or money belts; avoid crowded Metro stations.
2. **Language basics:** Learn simple phrases ("Excusez-moi", "Combien ça coûte?", "Où est…")—locals appreciate effort.
3. **Emergency numbers:** Police 112, ambulance 115, fire 114.
4. **Health:** Bring basic medications; pharmacies open 24h in most districts.

---

Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you’d like more tailored details—such as specific hotels, culinary experiences, or alternative itineraries—just let me know. Bon voyage!
